record.paper_title: A single impurity in an ideal atomic Fermi gas: current understanding and some open problems
record.original_question: For a single spinless impurity of mass M immersed in a zero-temperature 3D polarized atomic Fermi gas of background atoms of mass m with tunable s-wave impurity-background scattering length a, determine whether the dressed single-impurity branch called the polaron and the dressed branch connected to the impurity-background dimer called the dimeron are genuinely distinct energy branches, or instead the same branch connected continuously across the polaron-to-dimeron transition near k_F a ~ 1. In particular, determine whether the ground-state wave function is continuous across that transition and, in the small-m/M regime where the transition becomes continuous for a fixed impurity, whether the transition as a function of the mass ratio m/M is smooth at the critical 1/k_F a_c or remains discontinuous.

evidence.quote: We raise a few unsolved problems: whether the polaron and dimeron are really separate branches

Edwards [29] has raised the question of whether the polaron and dimeron energy branches are really separate or one and the same (i.e. is the groundstate wave function continuous across the polaron-to-dimeron transition at kFa ∼ 1?).
Is there a more definitive theoretical argument? Barring that, can we at least make a plausibility argument?
Is this a smooth transition at the critical 1/kF ac as a function of m/M: ... with α,β > 0? Or does it happen discontinuously?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a single spinless impurity of mass $M$ immersed at zero temperature in a three-dimensional, fully polarized ideal Fermi gas of background atoms of mass $m$ and Fermi wave number $k_F$. Assume the impurity interacts with the background atoms only through a short-range $s$-wave interaction characterized by a tunable scattering length $a$ (with all other partial waves negligible). As $1/(k_F a)$ is varied, two well-known dressed states of the impurity are usually distinguished:

(i) the "polaron" branch, the dressed single-impurity quasiparticle that is the ground state on the weakly attractive (BCS-like) side; 
(ii) the "dimeron" branch, the dressed state continuously connected to the bound impurity-background dimer that is the ground state on the strongly attractive (BEC-like) side.

For fixed mass ratio $m/M$, there is a critical value $1/(k_F a_c)$ at which the lowest-energy branch switches from polaron to dimeron.

Resolve the following questions:

(a) Are the polaron and dimeron genuinely distinct energy branches of the impurity Hamiltonian, or are they one and the same branch joined continuously through the transition near $k_F a \sim 1$? Equivalently, is the exact ground-state wave function continuous (in an appropriate Hilbert-space sense) across the polaron-to-dimeron crossing?

(b) In the regime of small $m/M$ (heavy impurity) where the transition at fixed mass ratio becomes continuous, decide whether, as a function of $m/M$ at the critical coupling $1/(k_F a_c)$, the transition is smooth — i.e. quasiparticle observables vary as $|m/M - (m/M)_c|^{\alpha}$, $|1/(k_F a) - 1/(k_F a_c)|^{\beta}$ with exponents $\alpha,\beta>0$ — or whether it remains discontinuous (first-order) for all $m/M>0$.

Provide a definitive theoretical argument, or, failing that, a rigorous plausibility argument settling (a) and (b).
artifact.status_search_result: The question of whether the polaron and dimeron are truly distinct branches and the precise nature of the transition (first-order vs. smooth, especially as a function of m/M) remains an open theoretical problem. Variational and diagrammatic Monte Carlo calculations in the continuum 3D case generally support a first-order ground-state transition for equal masses, but experiments observe a smooth crossover (attributed to finite temperature and impurity density). No rigorous proof of branch (dis)continuity or of the smoothness/discontinuity of the transition as a function of mass ratio at the critical coupling is available.

status_evidence.title: Observation of a Smooth Polaron-Molecule Transition in a Degenerate Fermi Gas
status_evidence.snippet: continuous variation of all observables ... smooth reduction of the quasiparticle weight ... smooth transition between polarons and molecules and coexistence
status_evidence.claim: Experimentally, a smooth crossover is observed, but this is attributed to finite-temperature/density effects rather than a resolution of the zero-temperature single-impurity question.

status_evidence.title: On polarons and dimerons in the two-dimensional attractive Hubbard model
status_evidence.snippet: polaron and dimeron ansatz ... ground state in BCS limit ... ground state in BEC limit
status_evidence.claim: Polaron and dimeron are typically described by distinct variational ansätze, and the question whether they are genuinely separate branches is still discussed.
